summary: Flathead NF 30-foot wooden live-in lookout built in 1932 on Napa Point; staffed in 1955, reached by road in 1967, and now gone.

events.note: 30-foot wooden live-in tower with two patrol points 1 and 1.25 miles away, per firelookout.com
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description names the Napa Forest Service lookout tower
Two men on horseback repaired storm damage at the lookout (July 1955 item)
John Dunn staying at the Napa lookout that summer
June 1968 item says the lookout became accessible by road the year before

evidence.supports: built 1932 as a 30-foot wooden live-in tower with patrol points, and marked gone
evidence.quote: 1932: 30' wooden live-in tower. Patrol points 1 mile ENE at 7100' and 1.25 miles NE at 7100'. Gone.

evidence.quote: John Dunn is staying at the Napa lookout this summer.

notes_for_editor: The 1932 build date and the 30-foot height rest on firelookout.com alone; height_m is converted from 30 feet. The weebly newspaper items are quoted secondhand. A trail page for the Napa Lookout Trail was not readable through fetch_text (AllTrails returned 403; the Hike Wild Montana page text was not extracted), so the site today is undescribed. Napa Point is not Little Napa Point (a different, standing NHLR lookout), which was not used. Brief record checked: county, agency, coordinates and gone status match the sources.
